target.title: fix(msteams): bound Graph attachment JSON responses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Microsoft Teams attachment recovery read successful Microsoft Graph message and hosted-content collection responses with unbounded `response.json()` calls. A buggy or hostile upstream response could therefore force the Gateway to buffer an arbitrarily large body.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both Graph JSON surfaces now use OpenClaw’s shared bounded provider-response readers:

- hosted-content collections use `readProviderJsonArrayFieldResponse`, which bounds the stream and validates the required `value` array;
- message metadata uses `readProviderJsonResponse`, preserving the existing warning and empty-attachment fallback on parse failure;
- oversized streams are cancelled at the shared 16 MiB cap;
- the changelog records the user-visible hardening and credits @cxbAsDev.

This is the plugin-owned boundary: authentication, SSRF policy, attachment byte limits, and downstream `$value` media reads remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Teams channel/chat attachment recovery can no longer exhaust Gateway memory by buffering unbounded Graph JSON. Normal Graph responses behave as before; malformed or oversized metadata degrades to no attachments and existing diagnostics.

## Evidence

- Exact reviewed head: `2c3a097cbee06962dfed4b77cfddd66647c6cc1f`.
- Sanitized public-network AWS Crabbox `cbx_3fc4771fd4d0` (no Tailscale or instance role), run [`run_558302b119aa`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_558302b119aa): `pnpm test extensions/msteams/src/attachments/graph.test.ts` — 13/13 passed.
- Fresh exact-head structured autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings (0.97).
- Regression coverage exercises oversized hosted-content collection and message metadata responses through the real shared bounded reader.
- Microsoft’s [hostedContents list contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/chatmessage-list-hostedcontents?view=graph-rest-1.0) returns metadata in `value` and retrieves bytes through the separate `$value` endpoint, matching the implementation boundary.

Not tested against a live tenant with an oversized Graph response: Microsoft does not provide a safe way to induce that malformed upstream condition. The transport behavior is exercised with real `Response` streams in the focused test.
